rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem`. Both carry {test} references to it.

**Constructor defaults and field preservation.** `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` builds an item with `OutlineItem::new`. It asserts the defaults: `name_span == None`, empty `attachments`, and `header_span` and `trailer_span` both `None`. After `with_header_span`, `with_trailer_span` and `with_name_span`, it asserts the header and trailer spans. After cloning the `Outline`, it asserts `selector`, `kind`, `span`, `structural_hash` and `name_span` all equal the supplied values.

**`with_attachments` sets the list.** The test calls `with_attachments` twice, first with a `Comment` and then with an `Annotation`. It asserts that only the second attachment remains, with its kind and span intact. A version that appended instead of replacing would fail this.

**`with_own_hash`.** `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` uses `CustomLanguage`, whose `outline` calls `.with_own_hash(...)` with the source minus the highlighted span. For the root, the test asserts `structural_hash() == "a hello z"`, so `with_own_hash` does not overwrite the structural hash. It also asserts `fingerprint().value == "a  z"` with scheme `custom-v2:own-v1`, so the own digest is the one used for the fingerprint. For the selected item, it asserts `structural_hash == "selected-digest"`.

**`name_span` default.** The `None` default and the `with_name_span` setter are both asserted in the first test.

**Clone and Debug.** The first test calls `item.clone()` and `outline.clone()`. It formats `{outline:?}` and `{item:?}`, which only compile if `OutlineItem` implements `Debug`.

**Public shape and `#[non_exhaustive]`.** The public API listing is covered by `tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]`. The integration tests build items only through constructors, which is consistent with `#[non_exhaustive]`.

**Delegated obligations.** The behavior of `Span`, `name_span` and `attachments` is cited context and is assessed under those requirements. This includes the `Span` indexing rule, which belongs to `requirements.sdk.outlines.Span`. Which item owns each attachment is language-provider behavior and belongs to `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments`.

I found no obligation of the subject that these tests would miss.

`trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.

A named item's `name_span` is `Some` with the span to highlight for its name
in the original source snapshot. The highlighted text may differ from the
name in the selector. Use `selector` to address the item. The file root and
anonymous items have `name_span` set to `None`. `OutlineItem::new` starts with
`None`. Language providers use `with_name_span` to set the highlight within
